claims.statement: For every ordinary path-star with m>=1 distinct branches of arities r_i in {2,3,4}, let N=sum_i r_i, q=N+1, alpha=N+2, L=1+z, G=1+2z, B_r=L^r+z, F_r=sum_(h=0)^(r-2)L^h, Q=product_i B_(r_i), H_i=product_(h!=i)B_(r_h), C=GQ, T_i=GF_(r_i)H_i, and P=C+zL^q. Coefficients and Delta_k f=f[k+1]-f[k] are integer-zero-extended; let x=min{k natural: Delta_k P<0}, including the terminal difference. Define A0=LQ+zL^N and Ai=G B_(r_i-1)H_i+zL^N. At every actual natural p with x+2<=p, 3p<2alpha+1, and 2p<=alpha, put j=p-2, delta=q-j, D_j=binom(N,j+1)-binom(N,j), and beta_x=binom(q,x)-binom(q,x-1). In the coefficient-conditioned product model for C, with root weights (1,2), branch-i weights [z^t]B_(r_i), and D=1[X_0=0]+sum_i(1[X_i=0]-(r_i-1)/(r_i+1)1[X_i=1]), one has E_j D=(j+1)C[j+1]/C[j]-(q-j)<2j-N-(j+1)beta_x/C[x]. At the same p the strict selectors are e0=1[Delta_p A0<0] and ei=1[Delta_p Ai<0], with b=e0+sum_i r_i ei and A=sum_i r_i ei T_i[j]; the endpoint retains one original tag and branch i retains its r_i original tip tags. The bound is independent of the selector outcome and does not assert selected MASS or payment.
claims.scope: Universal informal coefficient lemma on the exact ordinary path-star family only. It retains the actual least strict parent descent, terminal zero extension, all three actual-p guards, and the current-p strict selectors and original tag multiplicities. It is not a Lean award and does not imply the primary payment.
claims.reason: At x, the shifted-binomial increment beta_x is positive by the actual lower-half guards and Delta_x P<0 forces C[x+1]/C[x]<1-beta_x/C[x]. Positive-interval log-concavity makes C's adjacent ratios nonincreasing, so this bound propagates to j>=x; substituting into the exact conditional drift identity proves the displayed strict inequality.

claims.statement: For every ordinary path-star with m>=1, branch arities ri in {2,3,4}, N=sum_i ri, q=N+1, alpha=N+2, L=1+z, G=1+2z, Br=L^r+z, C=G product_i B_(ri), and P=C+zL^q, let x be the least natural k with Delta_k P<0 under integer zero extension, including the terminal difference. For every profile with at least one actual natural p satisfying x+2<=p, 3p<2alpha+1, and 2p<=alpha, exact coefficient enumeration through m<=40 found no case with E_x D greater than the fugacity-one value 1/3+sum_i(2-ri)/(2^ri+1), where D=1[X0=0]+sum_i(1[Xi=0]-(ri-1)/(ri+1)1[Xi=1]) under the degree-conditioned product model with root weights (1,2) and branch-i weights [z^t]B_(ri). The search checked 4,308 such profiles; this is finite evidence only.
claims.scope: Bounded coefficient-model evidence for m<=40 under the exact least strict first descent of P, including terminal zero extension, and all three actual-p guards x+2<=p, 3p<2alpha+1, and 2p<=alpha. At that same p the original-leaf polynomials are A0=LQ+zL^N and Ai=G B_(ri-1)Hi+zL^N, with Hi=product_(h!=i)B_(rh); the selectors are e0=1[Delta_p A0<0] and ei=1[Delta_p Ai<0]. The endpoint multiplicity is one and branch i retains its ri original tip tags; this drift comparison makes no assumption about or replacement of those selectors. It compares conditional drift at x only; it does not establish a universal conditional-to-unconditioned inequality, any p-rank payment bound, or a registered primary theorem.
claims.reason: The script independently constructs the factor polynomials with integer arithmetic, computes terminal-aware first descent and literal guards, and evaluates conditional drift as an exact rational; it checks the derivative identity on each included profile. The finite horizon cannot establish a general comparison.

limitations: The explicit correction beta_x/C[x] has no derived uniform lower bound strong enough here to replace the small-prefix certificates.
The finite occupancy search is bounded evidence, not a proof of any unconditioned-to-conditioned comparison.
No new universal selected-mass, endpoint-only exclusion, exact-ratio payment, or formal result is claimed.
